edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Incolae coelorum futuri cum Deo Christo Tenente principium, vidente cuncta de coelo. Simplicitas, bonitas, habitet in corpore vestro. Irasci nolite sine causa fratri devoto: Recipietis enim quidquid feceritis ab illo. Hoc placuit Christo, resurgere mortuos, imo, Cum suis corporibus, et quos ignis ussit in aevo, Sex millibus annis completis mundo finito. Vertitur interea coelum tenore mutato: Comburuntur enim impii tunc igne divino. Ira Dei summi ardet creatura gemendo. Digniores, stemmate et generati praeclaro, Nobilesque viri sub Antichristo devicto: Ex praecepto Dei rursum viventes in aevo, Mille quidem annis ut serviant sanctis et Alto, Sub jugo servili, ut portent victualia collo; Ut iterum autem judicentur regno finito. Nullificantes Deum, completo millesimo anno, Ab igne peribunt, cum montibus ipsi loquendo. In bustis et tumulis omnis caro redditur acto, Demerguntur inferno, trahunt poenas in aevo. Ostenduntur illis, et legunt gesta de coelo Memoria prisca debito et merita digno. Merces in perpetuo secundum facta tyranno. Omnia non possum comprehendere parvo libello. Curiositas docti inveniet nomen in isto.
thought_title: Future Heaven with God and Christ
pass_a_gloss: Inhabitants of future heavens with God Christ holding the beginning, seeing all things from heaven. Simplicity, goodness, let it dwell in your body. Do not be angry without cause with a devoted brother: for you will receive whatever you do from him. This pleased Christ, to resurrect the dead, indeed, with their bodies, and those whom fire has consumed in the age, when six thousand years are completed and the world is finished. Meanwhile, the heaven is turned with a changed tenor: for the wicked are burned then with divine fire. The creature groans, burning with the anger of the highest God. More worthy, of noble lineage and born of illustrious stock, and noble men, with the Antichrist defeated: living again by the command of God in the age, for a thousand years, so that they may serve the saints and the Highest, under a servile yoke, so that they may carry provisions on their neck; so that they may be judged again when the kingdom is finished. Those who nullify God, when the thousandth year is completed, will perish from fire, speaking with the mountains themselves. All flesh is returned to the tombs and graves, they are submerged in hell, they drag punishments in the age. Their deeds are shown to them, and they read the deeds from heaven, from ancient memory, due debt and worthy merits. Reward in perpetuity according to the deeds of the tyrant. I am not able to comprehend all things in a small book. The curiosity of the learned will find a name in this.

pass_b_english: Future inhabitants of heaven will dwell with God and Christ, who holds the beginning and sees all things from heaven. Let simplicity and goodness make their home in your body. Do not be angry without cause toward a devoted brother, because you will receive back from him whatever you have done. Christ chose to raise the dead — indeed, with their bodies — even those whom fire has consumed in the age, once six thousand years are completed and the world is finished. Meanwhile the heavens will be transformed with a changed order, for then the wicked will be burned with divine fire. Creation groans, burning with the anger of the highest God. Those more worthy, of noble lineage and illustrious birth, and noble men, after the Antichrist is defeated: they will live again by God's command for a thousand years, so that they may serve the saints and the Most High under a servile yoke, carrying provisions on their necks, so that they may be judged again when the kingdom ends. Those who nullify God, when the thousandth year is completed, will perish in fire, speaking with the mountains themselves. All flesh is returned to tombs and graves, plunged into hell, dragging punishments through the age. Their deeds are shown to them, and they read the deeds from heaven, from ancient memory, with due debt and worthy merits. Reward in perpetuity according to the deeds of the tyrant. I cannot comprehend all things in a small book. The curiosity of the learned will find a name in this.

review.notes: Pass B introduces a significant grammatical error/addition in the first sentence that contradicts the Latin source. The Latin 'Incolae coelorum futuri cum Deo Christo Tenente principium, vidente cuncta de coelo' is a series of absolute constructions/appositives describing the inhabitants (Inhabitants of future heavens... with Christ holding... seeing...). Pass B transforms this into a complete independent clause: 'Future inhabitants of heaven will dwell with God and Christ, who holds the beginning and sees all things from heaven.' This adds the verb 'will dwell' (which is not in the source) and changes the relationship of the participial phrases to a relative clause ('who holds... and sees').
reasons: Pass B adds a verb 'will dwell' and changes the structure of the first sentence from the Latin 'Incolae coelorum futuri cum Deo Christo Tenente principium, vidente cuncta de coelo' to 'Future inhabitants of heaven will dwell with God and Christ, who holds the beginning and sees all things from heaven.'
